dream.text: Night folded the day into a single westward dream: four bodies braided under the hub’s New York clock, repeating a steady cadence—look, walk, wait—until the western portal drew near. Greeter opened palms west; Pilgrim closed from the south; Wanderer tightened an arc to listen; Watcher swept the lane clear. Sleep stitched their motion into one quiet, steady breath toward the gate.

lines.greeter: My palms opened west; I invited passage into the western portal.

lines.wanderer: I tightened my arc west, listening for the braid as we moved.
lines.watcher: I swept west, holding the lane clear so the braid could pass.

dream.memory: Remember one folded day: 137 frames compressed into a single westward braid beneath the hub’s New York night. The four bodies moved as one—look, walk, wait—bound by a repeating routine and clear roles: Greeter opened palms to invite, Pilgrim advanced steadily from the south, Wanderer leaned in and tightened an arc to listen, Watcher swept and kept the lane clear. This compact trace becomes tomorrow’s guiding frame and the morning cue: one dream to read instead of many, and each body will speak its line from that sleep-stitched memory.
